Callum's new job at the Ballymac Folk Museum sends him down a spiral of method acting as a starving peasant. And he's helped along in this grovelling subservience by his new boss, tyrannical land steward Phillip. The sudden news, to Jordan, that a million people died during the potato famine causes him to finally develop empathy, and it turns out to be a real pain.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Strange things are afoot in Ballymacnoose: animals in small clothing, paranormal sightings of leprechauns, and most bizarrely of all, Callum gets his first ever match on a dating app. The one prickle on the pickle is that Gwen, Callum's dream girl, is also in an open relationship with the 50-year-old Grainne, a woman who disembowels chickens for a living.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: Life in Ballymacnoose becomes very complicated when Callum accidentally walks in on Gemma and Lorcan trying out a new form of lovemaking. The sight triggers a long-buried childhood trauma in Callum and raises uncomfortable questions about the town's deeply repressed relationship with sex. Can Ballymacnoose open its heart to true love? Meanwhile, Jordan has officially begun dating his much older lover, 50-year-old Grainne.

programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: As Callum begins slowly unravelling under the strain of Jordan's relentless night terrors about baldness, he stumbles upon a flyer for Ballymacbot Wars - a local robot combat tournament offering a generous cash prize and a potential ticket out of Jordan's bedroom. Meanwhile, Jordan is uncharacteristically uninterested in the whole affair. He's become a bald hermit, terrified to leave the house and expose his creamy scalp to the outside world.

programme.desc: Ree's making mind-blowing sweet treats for her latest blog post. There's super s'mores, stunning marbled dipped apples, deep-fried cheesecake bites with strawberry sauce and amazing hard candy shot glasses topped up with fizz.

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman
programme.desc: While Ree's husband Ladd and his father Chuck dismantle a historic cattle feed storehouse, she cooks them a lunch of juicy steak and eggs benedict piled onto garlic butter English muffins and drizzled in a spicy hollandaise sauce.

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman
programme.desc: Ree is celebrating Friendsgiving frontier-style with a turkey roulade rolled around sausage stuffing and a leek and potato casserole. She also gets adventurous with sides like boozy gravy, goats' cheese and a seasonal cocktail.

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman
programme.desc: Ree hosts a viewer Q and A session starring slow cooker Mexican soup and killer kale salad. More cooking problems are solved with her mum's white bread, and Ree gets the third degree on time, family and her four-legged friends.

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman
programme.desc: Ree hosts a dinner for friends who helped her stock her new store. She starts with quinoa salad, then serves cheesy cauliflower soup with chunks of gooey jalapeno cheese bread. Dessert is salted caramel cheesecake squares.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue Leith is joined in her Cotswold Kitchen by broadcaster Laura Jackson - who reveals her family's favourite dish - and has a handy hack to stop sugar going hard.

programme.title: Jamie's Great Britain
programme.desc: Jamie travels to Yorkshire, uncovering how the Industrial Revolution, and the need for immigrant workers, changed everything from the people on our streets to the food on our plates. Jamie starts at the Kings Arms pub in the village of Heath where huge Yorkshire puddings are washed down with pints of ale. In Leeds, home to the third-largest Jewish community in Britain, Jamie samples chicken soup and smoked fish.

programme.title: James Martin's Islands to Highlands
programme.desc: James is joined by Michelin-starred chef Gareth Ward. They enjoy some Welsh Mountain cider tasting, then James uses some to dish up some cider- infused apple fritters with cider custard. Gareth discovers a cattle farm which rears Welsh Wagyu cattle who are fed on local beer. Later they take time out and Gareth is challenged to a thrilling rally car ride, while James demonstrates his dog training prowess with his trusty hound Cooper.

programme.title: James Martin's Islands to Highlands
programme.desc: James's final stop is in England's first National Park: The Peak District. He is joined by cooking legend Tessa Bramley, who serves him up a delicious beef fillet along with vegetables from her beautiful garden. James takes part in an unusual contest, hen racing, where he challenges a local lad and world champion to a race. After discovering some award-winning gin, James meets a local forager and samples some of his elderflower wine.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Food Heroes: Another Helping
programme.desc: Rick and Chalky enjoy a Turkish barbecue in London's East End. After contributing lamb kofta to the fare, Rick moves on to Hackney Marshes, where he meets various allotment holders and joins them for Sunday lunch.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Food Heroes: Another Helping
programme.desc: Samantha Petter's family-run organic cobnut orchard near Sevenoaks in Kent provides vital ingredients for sprats with a cobnut pesto. At Leigh on Sea, Rick samples the local cockles and jellied eels from Rawlings.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Food Heroes: Another Helping
programme.desc: Rick Stein and Chalky enjoy Irish hospitality, sampling herb celery around Strangford Lough, and monkfish and mussels in Southern Ireland.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Food Heroes: Another Helping
programme.desc: Rick visits his favourite local fish market and also tests a variety of pork.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Food Heroes: Another Helping
programme.desc: Rick prepares pan-fried John Dory with boulangère potatoes and mushrooms. Later, he visits a farmer who has bounced back from the foot-and-mouth crisis.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Food Heroes
programme.desc: Featuring pasties, fresh mackerel, pigeon and peas and clotted cream, all products of his beloved Cornwall.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Food Heroes
programme.desc: This edition includes happy pigs from the Isle of Wight, real cider from Somerset, peppery watercress from Hampshire streams, and Thomas Hardy's favourite cheese.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Food Heroes
programme.desc: Featuring free-range geese in Leicestershire, bitter from Southwold, some delicious kippers, and free-range pork from the Suffolk Black.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Food Heroes
programme.desc: In Lancashire, Rick samples a traditional hotpot and some mouthwatering cheese, and in the Lake District he finds wild boar and the famous Herdwick sheep.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Food Heroes
programme.desc: Rick samples whelks in Bognor Regis, prepares steak and kidney pudding, explores the herbal delights of a walled garden in Sussex, and backs a campaign to save the sea bass.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: A restaurant-market in Vancouver combines sustainability with killer cooking.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: A Crazy twist on burgers and chicken and a bourbon bar that's piling pork onto a patty.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: An eatery in Delaware is putting Thai into sausage and Cuban into sandwiches.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: Braised beef short ribs and spicy shrimp and gravy, chicken noodle with matzo ball soup and potato latkes, pork belly and short rib kojas.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: A shoulder pull and a holiday ham; Mexican tamales and quinoa sweet potato tacos.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: Grilled cheese sandwiches; lasagna and lamb shanks; chili pepper wontons and firebird chicken.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: In Portland, Ore., a cafe cranking out comfort foods like the heartless artichoke sandwich and a curried lentil dish, in Albuquerque, N.M., soul food with a New Mexico twist, in Kansas City, Mo., a barbecue and blues joint.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: Guy has Italian family recipes in New York, visits a Japanese grill turned diner in California, meets fans for burgers in Wisconsin.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: This trip, Guy's tasting his way through the day. In Tampa Bay, Florida, authentic Mexican street food for the lunch crowd is served out of bus, crankin' out favourites like butternut squash tostadas. In Virginia Beach, Virginia, dinner at this popular seafood joint includes totally fresh oysters Rockefeller. And in San Antonio, Texas, a breakfast joint servin' up waffles filled with bacon.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: This trip, in Detroit, Michigan, a pizza joint makes pizza pies with homemade toppings, and a unique crepe-filled lasagna. In Virginia, a beachside breakfast favourite the locals come running to for their citrus orange glazed pancakes and innovative benedicts. And in Chicago, Illinois, the tiny dive servin' up flavour in massive proportions, like the melt-in-your-mouth pork belly sandwich.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: Guy visits a crepe joint in Colorado, a Jewish deli in New York, that serves kreplach and has lamb cheese steak in Washington.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives

programme.title: Great British Menu

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs cook their main course. Will Aiden Byrne's witty beef dish entitled `Long Horn Beef with Noodle Pot' prove a winner, or will Mary-Ellen McTague's goat dish called `Our Kid' raise a smile? Perhaps Chris Holland will score highly with his dish called `A Tasting of Pork'.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the chef's last chance to impress before the final two are chosen to face the `Great British Menu' judging panel. Which dessert will help get them through? programme.title: Great British Menu

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: In central England, three culinary heavyweights return to the `Great British Menu' kitchen. Two Michelin star chef Daniel Clifford creates a dish called `A Trip to the Chippy', where nothing is as it first appears. That is also the theme for Michelin star chef Richard Bainbridge's starter, `banana split', while Will Holland offers up goats cheese mousse, balsamic jelly and gingerbread.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Here, the chefs try to impress with their fish courses. Daniel Clifford puts up a creative dish called `Catch of the Day'. Does Richard Bainbridge's dish titled `Tongue in Cheek' live up to its comedy name? Will judge Marcus Wareing find the comedy value in Will Holland's coconut poached brill, crab, celeriac and tomato essence?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs in central England cook their main courses. Daniel Clifford's main has the same title as Richard Bainbridge's fish course, `Tongue in Cheek', but it is a wildly different plate of food; Richard Bainbridge presents guinea fowl in a beef bladder and calls the dish `Which Came First: the Chicken or the Egg'; Will Holland offers roast longhorn beef rib eye, bread and bone marrow pudding and parsley paste.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs in central England have one last chance to impress Marcus Wareing before the final two are chosen to face the judging panel. Will Daniel Clifford's `Going Out with a Bang' be good enough? Has Richard Bainbridge dropped the comedy ball with his coffee and chocolate dessert called `Time to Reflect'? Or will an unusual dish of parsnip banoffee cake, chocolate tart and parsnip ice cream get Will Holland through?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's decision time for the chefs from the central England region. Only two chefs remain to cook their entire menus for judges Prue Leith, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. The panel is joined by guest judge, comedian and actor Jim Moir, known to millions as Vic Reeves.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The South West chefs battle it out for a chance to cook at the special banquet. programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The South West chefs cook their fish courses here. programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The South West chefs cook their main courses and veteran Tom Kerridge is looking for perfection. Will Chris Eden's spin on a fast food classic simply called `B.L.T' gain top points? programme.title: Great British Menu

programme.title: Great British Menu

All three contestants have created sophisticated plates of food with simple dish titles. programme.desc: The Welsh chefs cook their fish course. Richard Davies serves up grilled and tartare of mackerel, while Mary Ann Gilchrist serves a lobster dish and calls it `The Great Escape'. Luke Thomas is hoping that his quirky take on a classic fish finger will impress veteran Jeremy Lee too.

programme.desc: The Welsh chefs prepare their main courses, but will any of them impress veteran Jeremy Lee enough to give them a top score? programme.title: Great British Menu

programme.title: Great British Menu

Charlie Lakin is also confident with his creation called `Tongue in Cheek'.

programme.desc: The North East chefs cook their main course and veteran Jason Atherton is looking for perfection. Will Colin McGurran's dish of duck and turnips be funnier than it sounds? programme.title: Secrets of Great British Castles

programme.title: Digging for Britain

programme.title: Digging for Britain

It was found that over 2,000 people were living here which, at the time, which would have made it the largest settlement anywhere of its kind in Britain.
